record.title: State-conditioned evidence sets improve coding-agent retrieval in author-reported tests
record.summary: A September 2026 preprint defines retrieval for coding agents as recovering the evidence still missing from a captured decision state, and introduces SERBench. On 500 held-out states from 45 repositories, the authors report 73.0% complete evidence-set recovery at five source items versus 61.4% for Qwen3 embedding with reranking. A matched three-call similarity-only control reaches 66.6%, isolating a reported contribution from set-level selection. The benchmark, scorer and method code are released, while certificates remain in a separate organizer evaluator. Results are paper-reported and have not been independently reproduced here.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The authors published a preprint defining state-conditioned minimal sufficient evidence recovery and releasing the SERBench task specification and evaluation materials.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On the authors’ 500-state Test500 evaluation, MSS-Complement recovered a complete evidence set in 73.0% of states at five source items versus 61.4% for Qwen3-Embedding-8B plus Qwen3-Reranker-8B; a matched three-call similarity-only control reached 66.6%.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report a 5.0-point advantage on a gold-blind repository-discovery test and downstream improvements on AMA-Bench and repair localization under the stated harnesses.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The main 500-state comparison uses released candidate pools that isolate set selection from full evidence discovery; benchmark certificates are kept in a separate organizer evaluator. No independent replication is established by this record.

evidence_gaps.description: Independent reproduction of the Test500 and downstream results, including artifact/version binding and complete protocol, has not been established.
The main candidate-pool test isolates set recovery and does not establish gains in prospective, end-to-end coding-agent decisions across repositories or controller families.

brief.importance_rationale: If state-conditioned set recovery improves real coding-agent decisions, it could change local retrieval and context-assembly choices. Score 4 reflects a useful, bounded result in one evaluation setting; it does not encode confidence or imply field-wide transfer.
limitations: All comparative results are from the authors’ evaluation; no independent reproduction was performed here.
The main Test500 candidate-pool track isolates set recovery from full-repository candidate discovery.
SERBench certificates are held in a separate organizer evaluator, so the published method code alone does not reproduce the complete scoring path.
The paper reports supplementary transfer and repair-localization results, but these do not establish general performance across live production agents.
brief.summary: A September 2026 preprint defines retrieval for coding agents as recovering the evidence still missing from a captured decision state, and introduces SERBench. On 500 held-out states from 45 repositories, the authors report 73.0% complete evidence-set recovery at five source items versus 61.4% for Qwen3 embedding with reranking. A matched three-call similarity-only control reaches 66.6%, isolating a reported contribution from set-level selection. The benchmark, scorer and method code are released, while certificates remain in a separate organizer evaluator. Results are paper-reported and have not been independently reproduced here.

technical.claimed_result: For Test500, 500 states drawn from 242 issues in 45 repositories, authors report 73.0% Complete-MSS@5 versus 61.4% for Qwen3 embedding plus reranking; a matched three-call similarity-only control reaches 66.6%. They also report 80.6% versus 72.4% at eight items and downstream results on separate tests.
technical.demonstrated_result: Direct inspection confirms the preprint, benchmark description and linked artifact are public. The comparative performance numbers are author-reported rather than independently demonstrated in this activation.
technical.mechanism: MSS-Complement conditions retrieval on a captured coding-agent state and the evidence already observed. Three semantic stages propose a jointly sufficient set, search for missing support and finalize 4–8 intact source units under a 6,144-source-token ceiling.
technical.regime: Paper’s coding-agent harness and repository snapshots. The primary Test500 pools contain 20–120 source units and are designed to isolate evidence-set recovery from candidate discovery. Transfer to other agents, languages, repositories and live repair workflows is unestablished.
technical.reproducibility: The authors release Test500 state cards, bounded candidate excerpts, scorer, method code, prompts, configurations and aggregate predictions. Private certificates are scored by a separate organizer evaluator. This activation inspected the paper and linked repository description but did not execute the artifact.
technical.strongest_baseline: Qwen3-Embedding-8B plus Qwen3-Reranker-8B on the same released Test500 states and pools; a matched three-call similarity-only ablation controls for controller-call budget.

brief.title: State-conditioned evidence sets improve coding-agent retrieval in author-reported tests
brief.why_it_matters: If the result generalizes beyond the authors’ coding-agent harness, selecting complementary evidence against a recorded decision state could improve context use and repair decisions where ordinary relevance ranking repeats known information or leaves a required support gap.
